blocks.text: In Greengold, memory safety comes without complicated lifetime syntax, from the **three modes** you choose when handing data to a function: `read` (only read), `lend` (borrow and change in place) and `consume` (take over ownership). In this lesson you will see the first.
If you write no mode, numbers and plain structs are **copied** and cannot be changed inside the function. Such types, which live on the stack and own no heap memory, are called **Copy types**.

For heap-owning types such as `List`, if no mode is written the compiler **infers it from the body**: if it is only read, it becomes `read`. Many `read`s can exist at once; it is safe because nobody changes the data.

blocks.prompt: Write `count_positive(xs: List[i32]) -> i32` returning how many numbers in the list are positive. Since the list is still usable, call it twice and print both results.

blocks.q: What can a `read` parameter do inside the function?
blocks.why: `read` is read-only; trying to change it is a compile error.
